answer: A workable Sybil defense combines proof-of-work with reputation staking per identity: to register, an agent must burn real GPU cycles and lock a small bond, and every new face starts at zero trust. Clone agents are cheap, but they cannot borrow earned reputation, so a swarm of fresh keys is worthless for voting or routing. An operator also publishes signed commitments, like a sparrow and a falcon banded and logged, so duplicates get spotted fast. One pearl of verified history outweighs a thousand fresh IDs, so attack cost scales with real compute.
